However, the project faced a reported disagreement with Penguin Random House India regarding its contents before HarperCollins finalized an agreement to publish the Indian edition. Rahul Gandhi expressed pride in his mother's decision to share her story.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Launches Memoir on Instagram Amid Publishing Dispute

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram to share a first look at her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. The book chronicles her life from childhood in post-war Italy to her time in India. Publisher Alfred A. Knopf announced the release date as November 10. Rahul Gandhi expressed pride in his mother's story on his father's birth anniversary.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Launches Memoir on Instagram Amid Family Tributes

items.summary: Besi Semiconductor Industries reported third-quarter orders of €342.6 million, beating analyst expectations of €298 million driven by AI data-centre demand. CEO Richard Blickman dismissed reports that ASML is a hybrid bonding rival, stating the two companies collaborate. Besi also announced a €100 million share buyback and provided softer fourth-quarter revenue guidance.
items.title: Besi Beats Order Expectations on AI Demand, Denies ASML Rivalry

items.summary: Discussions between SpaceX and Tesla regarding a potential merger have drawn attention due to Elon Musk's involvement in both entities. Sources indicate that the companies are evaluating various transaction structures, including a merger under a new holding company. Concerns mirror those from Tesla's 2016 SolarCity acquisition, where Musk's role sparked litigation. Musk has acknowledged his conflict of interest and agreed to recuse himself from discussions. Legal experts note that Texas law, where Tesla is incorporated, introduces uncertainty compared to Delaware precedents. The potential deal, described as the largest in history, could face regulatory scrutiny and shareholder challenges.
items.title: SpaceX and Tesla Merger Talks Face Scrutiny Over Shareholder Concerns

items.summary: Singapore security robotics firm Kabam announced it will cease operations on November 20. The company, a subsidiary of Patec Group, thanked customers for their support but did not disclose reasons for the closure. Approximately 54 employees are associated with the firm, which previously deployed over 150 robots globally. Kabam was among the first six companies supported under Singapore's RoboNexus accelerator programme launched in March 2025.
items.title: Singapore robotics firm Kabam to cease operations by Nov 20

items.summary: Asian markets dipped on Oct 22 as investors weighed mixed tech earnings against Gulf tensions. While US tech stocks rose on strong results from SpaceX, Meta, and Super Micro, Asian indices fell. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index dropped 0.2%, and the Nikkei fell 0.4%. Concerns over AI spending and geopolitical risks in the Gulf, including US diplomatic orders to Saudi Arabia, weighed on sentiment. Treasury yields fell, and Brent crude rose near a five-month high.
items.title: Asian Markets Dip Amid Tech Earnings and Gulf Tensions

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 90th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March victory. Speaking on October 22, 2026, Xi emphasized that remembering history is essential for creating a brighter future. He noted the march covered more than 10 provinces between 1934 and 1936, calling it a feat of great significance for the nation's rejuvenation.
items.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses 90th anniversary of Long March victory

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on October 21, 2026. Li stated that China and Russia maintain close coordination to serve as a force for stability amid global turbulence. Putin noted that Russia-China relations are built on equality and mutual respect, unaffected by international changes. Both leaders emphasized deepening cooperation in energy, trade, and technology.
items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang Meets Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg

items.summary: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra shared an emotional message supporting her son Raihan Vadra after over 70 artworks were reportedly removed from his photography exhibition at Delhi's Bikaner House. Raihan alleged that management instructed him to remove images depicting protests and those featuring politicians, including his father Robert Vadra, citing alleged political content in the exhibition titled 'No Idea Is Final'.
items.title: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra Supports Son After Artwork Removals

items.summary: At the 140th Canton Fair, China's newest robots are showcased performing practical tasks rather than just demonstrations. The event features robot dogs fighting fires, machines lifting heavy loads, bots making coffee, and boxing robots. These machines are already doing real work, signaling a shift from mere exhibition to functional application in the industry.
items.title: China's Robots Move Beyond Displays to Real Work at Canton Fair

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah asserted that the Congress party will not form a government for the next 30 years, citing electoral defeats and double standards. This statement follows a controversy involving the removal of artworks from a Bikaner House exhibition by Rehan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. Shah also criticized the Aam Aadmi Party and highlighted the Bharatiya Janata Party's grassroots connection.
items.title: Amit Shah: 'Next 30 Years Congress Won't Form Govt, These Double Standards Won't Work'

items.summary: Ashok Reddy, Managing Director of the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board, inspected the Kokapet Green Water Filling Station. He instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically and to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker. Reddy also advised promoting purified water for construction and dust control to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.
items.title: Ashok Reddy Directs Online Water Quality Monitoring and Tanker Record Keeping

items.summary: A six-member special investigation team, led by retired Justice Anindita Roy Saraswati, is probing the deadly stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal that killed 19 people and injured 25. The panel aims to submit its report within three months, a duration Justice Saraswati noted as short but necessary. The investigation will examine the sequence of events, crowd capacity, and the response of various authorities to prevent future incidents.
items.title: Special Team Investigates Kolkata Stampede Within Three-Month Deadline

items.summary: Relatives of eight-year-old Elizabeth Struhs spoke at the final day of a coronial inquest into her death in 2022. The inquiry examined whether government agencies responded adequately to her child protection case before she died at home after her father stopped providing lifesaving insulin. Her parents and other members of the fringe religious group The Saints were recently acquitted of murder but found guilty of manslaughter, receiving prison sentences. Coroner Ainslie Kirkegaard thanked the family for sharing memories and stated she will reserve her decision, handing down findings in 2027.
items.title: Relatives speak at final day of inquest into Elizabeth Struhs death

items.summary: Jean-Marc Germain, a French MEP from the Socialists & Democrats group, stated that public order in France allows rioters to destroy shops and public buildings. He described the recent protests and violence as a big failure of the government. However, he does not believe Emmanuel Macron ought to resign, stating that it is elections that have to solve this issue, though he believes resolving issues with law and order are the condition for a good election process.
items.title: French MEP Jean-Marc Germain Criticizes Government Over Public Order

items.summary: The author posits that AI regulation will eventually exceed current levels, likely resulting in overregulation of the American economy. Consequently, the text suggests that AI might remain underregulated today to prevent future excesses. The author notes that regulatory issues fit within this framework and that overregulation has decades or centuries to catch up. The author believes most regulated economic sectors become overregulated.
items.title: Author argues AI may face future overregulation and suggests current underregulation

items.summary: Australia faces a monumental batting challenge to salvage a draw in the second Test against South Africa at St George's Park. South Africa leads by 170 runs, with Australia needing a significant recovery after losing four wickets in their second innings.
items.title: Australia battles to avoid defeat in second Test against South Africa

items.summary: India and Canada are rebuilding strained diplomatic and economic relations driven by shifting geopolitics and trade interests. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to visit Canada, following a reciprocal trip by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Both nations aim to finalize a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by year-end and target USD 50 billion in bilateral trade by 2030. The reset addresses past tensions regarding the Khalistan issue and US-Canada trade disputes. Canada seeks to diversify its trade partners, while India looks to secure energy and uranium supplies. A long-term uranium supply agreement worth USD 1.8 billion was signed to support India's nuclear power needs.
items.title: India and Canada Reset Ties Amid Geopolitical Shifts

items.summary: CCTV footage released to a jury shows Beau Lamarre-Condon visiting a McDonald's drive-thru in a van allegedly used to dispose of bodies. The 31-year-old officer is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in February 2024. Defence lawyer John Stratton SC claims Lamarre-Condon acted in self-defence and subsequently panicked, cleaning the scene and disposing of the bodies.
items.title: CCTV footage shows accused murderer visiting McDonald's drive-thru

items.summary: Barclays reported a 12% rise in quarterly pre-tax profits to £2.3bn, distributing an additional £500m to shareholders. The bank prepares for an upcoming UK bank tax increase announced in the October budget. Critics argue these profits stem from rising interest rates and mortgage costs, while the government seeks revenue for cost-of-living support.
items.title: Barclays Reports Profit Jump Amid UK Tax Hike Plans

items.summary: Protesters in Manipur marked the third day of sit-ins and mass cease-work following the killing of three Meiteis. Clashes between Meiteis and Kukis have left at least 50 people dead recently, with over 360 deaths since 2023. Families claim attackers were Kuki, while security forces dispersed crowds using tear gas and stun grenades. Tensions remain high as demands for justice persist.
items.title: Protesters in Manipur Mark Third Day of Cease-Work Amid Ethnic Violence

items.summary: German renewable energy producer Encavis has signed its first hybrid power purchase agreement combining solar and wind generation. The deal supplies Spanish company Visalia with 60 GWh of renewable electricity annually over three and a half years. The electricity originates from Encavis' Aragón portfolio near Zaragoza, comprising two solar parks and three wind farms with a combined capacity of 199 MW.
items.title: Encavis Signs First Hybrid Solar-Wind PPA with Spanish Supplier Visalia

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that Iranian oil in floating storage has been drained as the U.S. reimposed a naval blockade following the collapse of a ceasefire deal. Kpler data indicates storage fell from 150 million barrels to 866,000 barrels by mid-October. While the U.S. aims to pressure the regime, Iran's central bank governor claims the economy remains resilient despite record fuel prices and war costs estimated at $265 billion for U.S. households.
items.title: U.S. Naval Blockade Drains Iranian Oil Reserves Amid Escalating Tensions

items.summary: The States of Guernsey announced a new savings scheme providing £10 weekly for children in care until age 18. Established by the States' Children and Family Community Services and Guernsey Community Savings, the initiative aims to support young people's transition to independent living. Initially, 40 children will benefit immediately. Officials state the accounts offer financial security and choice as these individuals approach adulthood.
items.title: Guernsey launches £10 weekly savings scheme for children in care

items.summary: Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korea's leader, stated that anti-South Korea loudspeakers would be placed on standby along the entire border within days. She warned Seoul of a "most horrible and distressing situation" if South Korea continued interference in North Korea's internal affairs. Kim noted that activation would occur by the end of October following visits to fortification sites.
items.title: Kim Yo Jong Warns South Korea of Border Loudspeaker Activation

items.summary: Emerson Europe states that Europe's power sector is undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by renewable growth and rising demand from data centres. The company notes that many ageing thermal power plants must now provide flexibility and reliability alongside renewables, a task complicated by constrained budgets and personnel shortages. Emerson argues that modernisation, combining advanced control systems, software, and artificial intelligence, offers an alternative to replacing assets. The firm highlights how targeted upgrades can improve efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and extend plant lifespans, citing examples where automation reduced fuel use and improved operational performance.
items.title: Emerson Proposes Modernising Thermal Power Assets for Flexible Energy Needs

items.summary: The 2026 Ramnath Goenka Sahithya Samman announced shortlists for four categories: Fiction, Nonfiction, Debut, and Lifetime Achievement. The jury includes MP Shashi Tharoor, Sanjeev Sanyal, Vikram Sampath, and others. Winners will be declared on December 2. Notably, two titles originally absent from the longlist, Ashwin Sanghi's fiction and Shaan Kashyap's nonfiction, have been added to the shortlist.
items.title: Ramnath Goenka Sahithya Samman 2026 Shortlists Announced

items.summary: A landslide near Parassala railway station in Kerala derailed the Bilaspur-Tirunelveli Express early Thursday, disrupting services. Southern Railway confirmed all passengers and staff were safe. The incident occurred at 2:19 am following heavy rainfall, prompting an orange alert from the India Meteorological Department. Six passenger trains were cancelled, and the affected express train will now terminate at Neyyattinkara. Restoration work is underway.
items.title: Landslide Derails Train in Kerala Causing Service Disruptions

items.summary: Oil prices advanced following deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia that heightened concerns about Middle East supply disruptions. Brent climbed near $111 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate rose toward $99. Although a drone strike on the Shaybah field killed two people, operations remained unaffected. The global benchmark has surged more than 80% this year after Persian Gulf flows were disrupted by the ongoing U.S.-Iran war.
items.title: Oil Prices Rise Amid Saudi Attacks and Supply Fears

items.summary: North Korea announced it will resume anti-South Korea propaganda broadcasts along the heavily armed border, a move confirmed by leader Kim Jong Un's sister, Kim Yo Jong. The announcement follows recent land mine blasts that injured three South Korean soldiers, which North Korea denied responsibility for. Kim Yo Jong stated that loudspeakers for psychological warfare will be operational along the whole border within October. She also threatened retaliation against any South Korean provocation. South Korea's military responded by ordering stern measures and calling the threats intolerable. The border has seen 50 crossings by North Korean soldiers this year during fortification work, which Seoul blames for the recent explosions.
items.title: North Korea Announces Resumption of Anti-South Korea Propaganda Broadcasts Amid Rising Tensions

items.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was reportedly fined ₹50,000 by Customs officials at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport after returning from Paris. Sources cited undeclared luxury goods, including shoes, suits, and perfumes, as the reason. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) alleged the stoppage was politically motivated, claiming Mann was detained for three hours under pressure. Conversely, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused AAP of playing a victim card, stating Mann brought undeclared items worth ₹2.5 lakh in shoes and other valuables during a vacation. Both parties exchanged sharp words regarding the incident and the Centre's handling of the state's foreign travel permissions.
items.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann Fined at Delhi Airport Amid Political Row

items.summary: France's National Assembly economic affairs committee adopted an amendment to remove Article 82 from the 2027 budget bill, which would have altered existing solar power contracts. The amendment, led by Julie Laernoes and co-signed by 35 lawmakers, aims to prevent early termination of contracts signed between 2006 and 2010. The government seeks to save approximately €120 million through these measures, but the French Renewable Energy Association opposes the changes, citing the scheme's significant economic impact. The amendment requires further approval from the full parliament before implementation.
items.title: French lawmakers propose removing solar contract changes from 2027 budget

items.summary: The Opposition INDIA bloc is discussing further protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following a rally on November 1 at Delhi's Ramlila Ground. Options under consideration include a mock Parliament to enact Kumar's impeachment and a large march through central Delhi. CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby stated that various ideas are being discussed to build on earlier mobilisation. A senior Congress leader noted there are no concrete plans yet, while another leader said the final strategy will be decided collectively by the bloc. The campaign focuses on allegations of mass disenfranchisement and demands for Kumar's resignation.
items.title: INDIA bloc plans protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar

items.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Washington is not negotiating with Iran, asserting that a resolution will occur fairly soon. Meanwhile, Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia, and Pakistan signed a new defense cooperation pact in Doha. An attack on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport killed one person and injured eight. Russia released American citizen Stefan Hubbard, who had fought with Ukrainian forces. In sports, Harry Kane scored in a 2-2 draw between Bayern Munich and Arsenal, while Galatasaray defeated Lille 4-2 in the Champions League. Additionally, Barcelona reported PSG to UEFA over a controversial banner, and a US judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties.
items.title: Trump Halts Iran Talks; Global Defense and Tech News

items.summary: An attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight others, according to Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority. The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) stated that wounded individuals were transported to local hospitals. Flightradar24 reported flight diversions. Authorities did not identify the attackers. The incident occurred amid ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and facilities. In response to escalating attacks, the US State Department ordered diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, with plans to withdraw family members from other regional missions as well.
items.title: Attack on Saudi Airport Kills One, Injures Eight; US Evacuates Diplomats

items.summary: Delhi Police summoned Cockroach Janata Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka for questioning regarding trespassing and disobeying orders during an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar. Released from Tihar Jail on October 21 after furnishing bonds of Rs 50,000 each, the leaders must report to the Crime Branch. Two FIRs were transferred to the branch for further investigation.
items.title: Delhi Police Summon CJP Leaders Over Jantar Mantar Protest

items.summary: Residents of Pavlohrad, a Ukrainian city near the front line with Russia, describe daily life under relentless drone and missile strikes. While some express weariness and a desire for peace talks, they firmly reject Russian occupation, fearing it would lead to further territorial demands. Interviews with locals and a soldier highlight the psychological toll of the war and the strategic importance of the city. The article notes that since January 2025, US President Donald Trump has criticized Ukrainian leadership, adding to the complex political landscape. Despite the heavy atmosphere and frequent alerts, residents maintain their determination to remain in Ukraine.
items.title: Residents of Pavlohrad Resist Occupation Amid Relentless Bombardment

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer ordered legal action against officials following Congress allegations of irregularities in the Pilibhit Sadar Assembly constituency voter list. Congress claimed over 16,000 names were affected, including changes and deletions. The officer removed two officials and directed a district-wide review. This occurs amid broader protests against the Election Commission regarding the voter roll revision process.
items.title: UP Chief Electoral Officer Orders Investigation After Congress Alleges Voter List Irregularities

items.summary: In Israel's upcoming general election, Arab parties could secure a critical balance of power, potentially influencing the formation of the next government. Polls suggest neither Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor Gadi Eisenkot's Change Bloc has a clear path to a majority, with Arab-majority groupings holding around 13 to 14 seats. Driven by disaffection with the current government and issues like gang crime, Arab citizens are urged to vote. However, forming a coalition remains difficult as Eisenkot has ruled out working with Arab parties due to differing values. Meanwhile, Netanyahu's campaign has accused rivals of seeking to form a 'dangerous government' by teaming up with Arabs.
items.title: Arab Parties May Hold Balance of Power in Israeli Election

items.summary: Crude oil prices surged above $111 per barrel following reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi targets, including an oil field and an airport. Brent crude traded at $111.10, while West Texas Intermediate reached $98.98, both up around 2% from Wednesday. Iranian officials expressed skepticism about US sincerity in peace talks, citing past attacks during negotiations, suggesting the peace prospects remain slim.
items.title: Oil Prices Rise as Houthi Attacks on Saudi Targets Escalate

items.summary: Roslynn Garner-Gatley, 76, says she is frightened to use heating because domestic oil costs have nearly doubled. She relies on oil in Yealmpton, south Devon. Minister for Energy Consumers Polly Billington notes fuel costs rose by up to 82% since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran. Local councils offer crisis funds to struggling households.
items.title: Woman fears heating costs due to oil price surge

items.summary: Airbnb has implemented new global rules effective November 20, prohibiting hosts from requesting guests to perform tasks requiring significant effort, such as stripping beds or washing dishes. While cleaning fees remain, hosts must now factor costs into the total price. The platform clarified that reasonable requests depend on local conditions, allowing hosts to set seven standard house rules while banning confusing or onerous demands.
items.title: Airbnb Updates Global Rules to Limit Guest Chores

items.summary: AI infrastructure companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, and Cisco, warn UK ministers they have approximately 12 months to address public opposition to datacentre construction before facing US-style protests. A submission from the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) taskforce highlights rising scrutiny due to energy costs and environmental concerns. Microsoft has pledged $30bn (£22bn) for UK AI infrastructure. While the government notes measures to allow local authorities to retain business rates, campaigners argue these incentives may not suffice. Critics, including PauseAI UK and Action to Protect Rural Scotland, contend that tech companies are attempting to bypass community concerns and that public sentiment against hyperscale datacentres has already shifted significantly in the UK.
items.title: AI Firms Warn UK Has 12 Months to Prevent Datacentre Protests

items.summary: United Nations and Swiss officials met in Geneva to develop a plan to end the war in Sudan, which began in April 2023. Nearly two dozen countries attended, but the warring parties were absent. Officials described the conflict as a drone war causing famine and driving hunger, noting it has created the world's worst humanitarian crisis with over 34 million people in need and 11 million displaced.
items.title: UN and Swiss officials discuss plan to end Sudan war

items.summary: An author describes the decline of pitch deck quality, noting that most VCs and journalists now find AI-generated content annoying and indistinguishable. While the author expresses personal frustration with the format, a founder questioned why they should not use AI if VCs do. The piece highlights a growing consensus among investors against generic, AI-written decks, yet leaves the question of whether founders should abandon the format entirely open.
items.title: Investors Reject AI-Generated Pitch Decks as Founders Debate Utility

items.summary: Eternal shares jumped 2% after reporting a 77.6% year-over-year revenue increase to Rs 24,138 crore in the quarter. Brokerages like Jefferies and Morgan Stanley raised target prices, citing accelerating growth plans and improved unit economics. Management highlighted faster store expansion and strong performance in smaller cities as key drivers for the quick commerce sector.
items.title: Eternal Shares Rise on Strong Q2 Results and Brokerage Upgrades

items.summary: IHCL reported a 22% year-over-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 2,484 crore in the quarter. The company raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance by 300 basis points to 15-17%, driven by strong hotel segment revenue and robust demand for social and MICE events. IHCL signed 47 hotels in the first half of FY27, expanding its portfolio to 670 hotels. Brokerages Jefferies, Nomura, and Nuvama maintained or upgraded their ratings on IHCL shares, citing solid performance and asset upgrades translating into stronger pricing power.
items.title: IHCL Shares Rise on Revenue Beat and Raised FY27 Guidance

items.summary: The US Embassy in Ottawa accused Canadian officials of election interference ahead of the November midterms, citing plans to influence American politics. Canadian leaders, including Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford, dismissed these claims. The dispute involves trade tensions and retaliatory tariffs, with a petition against US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra gathering over 280,000 signatures.
items.title: US Embassy Accuses Canada of Election Meddling Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: France, Denmark, Finland, and the Netherlands took government websites offline Wednesday after web developers used AI to identify a bug affecting up to 70% of the world's websites. The exploit is described as the most severe AI vulnerability ever found. While fixes were released, researchers warn hackers may reverse engineer the bug in a race to exploit the public fix, potentially leading to the mass compromise of vulnerable web servers.
items.title: Governments Shut Down Sites After AI Finds Major Web Bug

items.summary: CATL shares plunged after the company reported slower-than-expected profit growth. Investors are concerned about expiring tax benefits and a trend called 'de-CATLization,' where customers like Xiaomi and Li Auto seek cheaper alternatives. Beyond domestic issues, CATL faces challenges in Europe due to rising protectionism. A UBS analyst noted that China's supply chain dependence is becoming less palatable.
items.title: CATL Shares Plunge on Earnings Miss and Competition Fears

items.summary: Rio Tinto and Rondo Energy are engineering a thermal energy storage system at Yarwun to store cheap midday electricity in hot bricks for later steam generation. The project aims to cut emissions by replacing coal and gas. A feasibility study, currently in progress, will assess technical and economic viability over the next 12 months.
items.title: Rio Tinto and Rondo Energy explore thermal battery for alumina refinery
